blogs.title: A Practical Guide to Vaccinating Your Dog or Cat
blogs.excerpt: Which vaccines actually matter, when to give them, and why your vet may recommend a different schedule than the internet does.
blogs.content:
Vaccination is one of the most studied interventions in veterinary medicine, and one of the most misunderstood by owners. Core vaccines protect against diseases that are either fatal, untreatable, or transmissible to humans — rabies being the obvious example. Non-core vaccines are recommended based on lifestyle: a dog that boards or visits parks needs different protection than one that lives indoors.

The right schedule depends on your pet's age, prior vaccination history, and local disease prevalence. Over-vaccination is a real concern; under-vaccination is a more dangerous one. The honest answer is that a short conversation with your vet is worth more than any blog post — including this one.
blogs.author: Dr. Bikash

blogs.title: Microchipping, Explained Without the Sales Pitch
blogs.excerpt: A microchip is the difference between a lost pet found and a lost pet gone. Here is what the procedure actually involves.
blogs.content:
A microchip is a passive RFID transponder roughly the size of a grain of rice, implanted under the skin between the shoulder blades. The procedure takes about ten seconds and is comparable in sensation to a vaccine injection. There is no battery, no GPS, and no maintenance.

When a lost pet is brought to any clinic or shelter, a handheld scanner reads a unique 15-digit ID. That ID maps to a contact record in a national registry. The system only works if you keep your details current — we will walk you through registration after the implant.
blogs.author: Dr. Bikash

blogs.title: When to Worry: Five Symptoms That Warrant a Same-Day Visit
blogs.excerpt: Pets are remarkable at hiding illness. These five signs are not ones to wait on.
blogs.content:
Sudden lethargy combined with reduced appetite is the most under-reported emergency we see. Repeated vomiting, particularly with blood or in a young puppy, can dehydrate an animal within hours. Difficulty urinating in a male cat is a true emergency — a blocked bladder is fatal in 24 to 48 hours.

Labored breathing, pale or blue gums, and any sudden collapse should be treated as emergencies regardless of the hour. When in doubt, call. We would rather reassure you on the phone than receive your pet too late.
blogs.author: Dr. Bikash

blogs.title: Choosing the Right Food: Beyond the Marketing
blogs.excerpt: Pet food labels are designed to sell, not to inform. A short guide to reading past the front of the bag.
blogs.content:
The most useful information on a pet food bag is on the back. Look for the AAFCO statement: it tells you whether the food is complete and balanced, and for which life stage. The ingredient list is ordered by weight before cooking, which means a 'chicken first' food may have less chicken than it appears once moisture is removed.

Price is a rough but imperfect proxy for quality. The best food is the one your pet does well on — stable weight, good coat, firm stools, normal energy. If those are present, brand wars are mostly noise.
blogs.author: Dr. Bikash
